body: [{"streamId":"01a0c941-fb35-749c-bcbb-4dba1666f51a","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Decision.DecisionRecorded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0c941-fb35-749c-bcbb-4dba1666f51a\u0022,\u0022Scope\u0022:\u0022Project\u0022,\u0022ScopeId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Statement\u0022:\u0022**A doctor check diagnoses the database, and it is the same check forever** (2026-08-23, backlog 24, extending #58\\u0027s teaching-not-guessing principle from install to every later moment \\u2014 database moved, container stopped, credentials rotated, laptop reimaged): four questions, answered in order, stopping at the first one that fails. (1) Is a connection string configured at all \\u2014 reads #73\\u0027s precedence chain and, only here, says nothing else has been checked yet. (2) Is it reachable \\u2014 a raw Npgsql connection attempt distinguishes \\u0060RefusedConnection\\u0060 (nothing listening) from \\u0060AuthenticationFailed\\u0060 (reached it, credentials rejected) from \\u0060DatabaseMissing\\u0060 (reached it, authenticated, wrong database name), because Npgsql\\u0027s own \\u0060PostgresException.SqlState\\u0060 already carries that distinction and conflating them was the one sin #58 named by name. (3) Is the schema there \\u2014 checked against \\u0060to_regclass(\\u0027public.mt_streams\\u0027)\\u0060, and answered as an offer rather than a warning, because Marten\\u0027s \\u0060AutoCreate.CreateOnly\\u0060 (every store in this platform already opens with it) creates it on first real use regardless; the offer just does that on the spot instead of the next command eating the latency. (4) Only reached when (1) failed: what is available \\u2014 a running container runtime, a native Postgres already on 5432 (a bare TCP connect, honest that it cannot tell Postgres apart from anything else on the port), and, the nicest possible finding, a **stopped** \\u0060hall9k-postgres\\u0060 container from a previous session, because \\u0022your database exists, it is just not running\\u0022 is a one-line fix and worth surfacing ahead of \\u0022go get Postgres.\\u0022 Question 4\\u0027s container probe speaks Docker\\u0027s CLI specifically (\\u0060docker info\\u0060, \\u0060docker ps\\u0060), while #57 keeps Podman, Apple\\u0027s container framework, and a native install equally valid Postgres hosts the same as always \\u2014 the probe covers the one runtime with a scriptable CLI convention worth automating; the others fall out through \\u0022point HALL9K_CONNECTION_STRING at whatever you already run.\\u0022 Every branch is a raw Npgsql connection attempt or a \\u0060docker\\u0060 shell-out \\u2014 no Wolverine host, no Marten codegen beyond the one schema-creation offer \\u2014 so it survives the thin-CLI rule (#8) even run before every database-touching command. It lives in \\u0060Hall9k.Cli\\u0060, never the daemon, for exactly that reason: it has to work while the daemon is down. \\u0060h9k doctor\\u0060 runs it on demand; \\u0060Program\\u0060\\u0027s top-level catch runs it \\u2014 offering no fixes, since a command mid-failure is not the moment to start Docker underneath it \\u2014 the instant any command\\u0027s \\u0060NpgsqlException\\u0060 or missing-configuration refusal reaches it, so the first raw failure a caller sees is already the diagnosis rather than a driver stack trace.\\n\\n**The offer is offer-never-force, the same shape as the auto-assign prompt at publish**, and it is where \\u0060h9k daemon start\\u0060 stops printing a lie: origin incident (2026-08-21), a post-restart \\u0060daemon start\\u0060 printed \\u0060h9kd started (pid N)\\u0060 and then, moments later, \\u0022exited during startup\\u0022 with an Npgsql stack trace, because Postgres was not back up yet \\u2014 a claim that had to be retracted before the human finished reading it. \\u0060DaemonLifecycle.StartAsync\\u0060 now runs the same doctor check **before** the log rotation, the detach, and the \\u0022started\\u0022 line, so an unreachable database refuses to spawn \\u0060h9kd\\u0060 at all rather than spawning it and reporting the death after. When the probe finds nothing listening, a container runtime running, and the host:port looks like the local default (\\u0060localhost:5432\\u0060, the one case Docker starting anything could plausibly fix), it asks \\u2014 \\u0022Found a stopped hall9k-postgres container\\u2026 start it now via Docker?\\u0022 or \\u0022Postgres isn\\u0027t running. Start it now via Docker?\\u0022 \\u2014 waits for readiness by polling the same raw connection attempt, and only then continues into daemon startup. A non-interactive invocation (\\u0060AnsiConsole.Profile.Capabilities.Interactive\\u0060 false, a script or a dispatched agent) gets today\\u0027s behavior: a named fix and a refusal, never a prompt nobody is there to answer. \\u0060h9k doctor\\u0060 offers the identical action for the identical reason \\u2014 the same check, run on demand instead of triggered by a failure.\\n\\n**The offer starts platform-owned infrastructure, and install stays boring anyway.** \\u0060h9k install\\u0060 writes Hall9k\\u0027s own Postgres definition \\u2014 a \\u0060docker-compose.yml\\u0060 mirroring the repository\\u0027s own, embedded in the binary \\u2014 to \\u0060~/.hall9k/postgres/docker-compose.yml\\u0060 on every publish-and-refresh (a local edit there is lost the next republish, deliberately: it is not a supported customization surface). Nothing is started and nothing is prompted for at install time; only the file lands, so \\u0060h9k daemon start\\u0060\\u0027s offer and \\u0060h9k doctor\\u0060\\u0027s offer never need a repo checkout to act on \\u2014 the thing #58 flagged as missing (an installed user has no dev worktree to run \\u0060docker compose\\u0060 from). The doctor\\u0027s own start-offer writes the same file as a belt-and-suspenders fallback for a CLI used straight off a dev build, without ever running \\u0060h9k install\\u0060.\\n\\n**Resolves \\u00A715 row 28: the two Postgres provisioning paths stay deliberately separate.** The Aspire AppHost (\\u0060dotnet run --project src/Hall9k.AppHost\\u0060) manages its own Postgres container for the dev loop through Aspire\\u0027s own APIs and injects a connection string directly into the daemon\\u0027s configuration (\\u0060builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString(\\u0022hall9k\\u0022)\\u0060), which \\u0060Hall9kDatabase.Resolve\\u0060\\u0027s \\u0060configured\\u0060 parameter treats as outranking even the environment variable \\u2014 Aspire\\u0027s wiring is a fourth, dev-loop-only channel, never one of the three precedence homes documented above. \\u0060h9k daemon start\\u0060, \\u0060h9k doctor\\u0060, and \\u0060h9k install\\u0060\\u0027s shipped compose file are installed mode\\u0027s own path and never touch Aspire\\u0027s container or vice versa; the two paths already bind the same port on purpose (so the default connection string works unmodified against either), which is why \\u0060docs/operations.md\\u0060 says to run one at a time rather than the platform trying to reconcile them.\\n\\n**Deliberately left for a refinement pass, named rather than silently skipped:** the symmetry question raised alongside this task \\u2014 does \\u0060h9k daemon stop\\u0060 offer to stop a container the start-offer started? A compose container outlives the daemon, and \\u0022what the offer starts, the mirror command should be able to end\\u0022 is a real design obligation this task does not close, because it needs the daemon to record *that* an offer started the container (versus finding it already running) before \\u0060stop\\u0060 can decide whether stopping it is its call to make. **Does this block the later vision?** No. The precedence chain, the container-name convention, and the shipped compose file are exactly the seams a stop-side mirror or a P2P-era per-node Postgres would build follow-up failed gate \\u0027test\\u0027 twice in one afternoon, both times the Testcontainers Postgres dying or losing its connection under the suite while the agent\\u0027s actual work was fine): \\u0060VerificationRunner\\u0060\\u0027s gate loop previously treated every non-zero exit identically, so a container hiccup and a genuinely broken build cost the same thing \\u2014 a failed run, a failed task, and a human\\u0027s diagnosis. \\u0060GateInfrastructureFailureClassifier\\u0060 applies the never-guess rule exactly as backlog 40 applied it to budget exhaustion: a fixed, narrow set of literal markers (Npgsql connection refused/reset/timeout exception types, \\u0022Exception while reading from stream\\u0022, \\u0022Failed to connect to\\u0022, the SSLRequest handshake mismatch, Testcontainers/Docker API failures) \\u2014 nothing fuzzier, so a test\\u0027s own assertion output never qualifies by coincidence. A gate whose failure classifies as infrastructure is retried once, in place: a new \\u0060GateRetried\\u0060 event records the gate and the cause on the run stream before the retry runs, so the record says the flake happened whichever way the retry goes, and the run is never failed nor is any budget spent on a flake the retry absorbs. A second consecutive infrastructure-classified failure fails the run honestly, the classification named in \\u0060RunFailed.Reason\\u0060, so a genuinely broken environment surfaces instead of looping; a retry that instead surfaces a real failure is recorded as exactly that, unclassified. Separately: \\u0060PostgresFixture\\u0060\\u0027s container already bound its host port at random by default (\\u0060PostgreSqlBuilder.Init()\\u0060 calls \\u0060WithPortBinding(5432, assignRandomHostPort: true)\\u0060), so the origin incident\\u0027s actual collision source was never a fixed mapping; the binding is now stated explicitly rather than left to the library default, and the likelier cause is named here rather than fixed, since the fix in scope was ephemeral ports, not test-suite parallelism: up to eleven \\u0060PostgresFixture\\u0060 instances can start concurrently under \\u0060dotnet test\\u0060 (ten of the twenty Postgres-backed test classes sit outside the serialized \\u0060Hall9kHome\\u0060 xUnit collection, each its own implicit collection xUnit runs in parallel by default), and Docker daemon contention under that many simultaneous container starts is a more plausible source of a dropped or garbled connection than the already-random port ever was. **Does this block the later vision?** No: the classifier and retry are entirely local to one daemon\\u0027s gate loop, and nothing about them assumes single-node project owns a home directory, created by a recipe rather than an agent** (2026-08-23, backlog 47, absorbing backlog 43; slice 1 of the project-centred structure, idea 64e4ebd2): a project\\u0027s files were scattered by convention rather than laid out by contract - the repository wherever it was cloned, ideas under a global \\u0060~/.hall9k/ideas\\u0060, runs under a global \\u0060~/.hall9k/runs\\u0060, and nothing at all tying them to the project they belong to. That was survivable while one machine had one project, and it is exactly what a second machine cannot reconstruct. **A project now records a home** (\\u0060ProjectHome\\u0060, a value object that refuses a relative path because the daemon reads it back from no particular directory), defaulting to \\u0060~/.hall9k/projects/\\u003Cname\\u003E\\u0060 and overridable at \\u0060project add\\u0060 or via \\u0060project set --home\\u0060; \\u0060h9k project show\\u0060 leads with it. **The shape inside it is the contract and the location is the setting**: \\u0060AGENTS.md\\u0060 (generated), \\u0060repo/\\u0060 (the bare clone, a \\u0060dev/\\u0060 worktree on the primary branch, and the \\u0060wt-*\\u0060 worktrees dispatch cuts beside them), \\u0060ideas/\\u0060, \\u0060tasks/\\u0060, \\u0060skills/\\u0060, plus a generated \\u0060.claude/\\u0060 adapter. There is deliberately **no top-level \\u0060runs/\\u0060**: a run belongs to exactly one task, so it lands under that task\\u0027s directory and the task directory is the task\\u0027s whole story (ruled during task refinement of backlog 49, which supersedes the six-entry list backlog 47\\u0027s own criteria were written from). **Creating it is platform code end to end** - the installation sitting\\u0027s words, restated at this discovery: \\u0022this is a recipe, not an agent\\u0022. Directories, bare clone, refspec correction, worktree, skill seeding and render are all deterministic, so \\u0060h9k project add\\u0060 does them at registration and \\u0060h9k project init\\u0060 is the adopt-and-repair path for a project without a home. Agents are reserved for the two judgment moments the discovery named: one-time migration of a nonconforming project, and configuration-laden tracker authoring. Neither is setup. **\\u0060repo/\\u0060 absorbs backlog 43\\u0027s recipe wholesale**, including the step that is the whole point of it: \\u0060git clone --bare\\u0060 writes \\u0060\\u002Brefs/heads/*:refs/heads/*\\u0060, mapping every remote branch onto a *local* branch, so a worktree cut from it has no upstream and \\u0060origin/main\\u0060 does not exist to branch \\u0060--no-track\\u0060 from. The refspec is corrected to \\u0060\\u002Brefs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*\\u0060, the local branches the bare clone invented are deleted, \\u0060core.longpaths\\u0060 is set on Windows, and a failed clone names \\u0060gh auth login\\u0060 / \\u0060gh auth setup-git\\u0060 rather than leaving an operator to guess. Every step is idempotent: an existing clone is reported and left alone, a missing \\u0060dev/\\u0060 beside one is repaired rather than treated as a reason to start over. **Init always materialises fresh from the recorded remote**, and an existing clone elsewhere on the machine is inconsequential - git is distributed, including across one disk - so the recipe never adopts one in place; once the clone is real the project is re-pointed at it, loudly, because a \\u0060repo/\\u0060 nothing dispatches against is decoration. Moving live work out of an old location stays the cutover chore\\u0027s agent-assisted job (backlog 52), which \\u0060--keep-repo-path\\u0060 exists to defer to. **The generated \\u0060AGENTS.md\\u0060 is a render, never a hand-maintained file** - the same one-way-render ruling the task and idea files get (backlog 48). It names the layout, points at the repository\\u0027s own \\u0060AGENTS.md\\u0060 as the deep layer rather than restating it, and lists the tool dependencies *derived from the project\\u0027s bindings*: \\u0060h9k\\u0060 and \\u0060git\\u0060 always, \\u0060gh\\u0060 when the remote is GitHub, the Atlassian CLI when a Jira board is bound. Deriving rather than declaring is what makes \\u0022rewritten when the facts change\\u0022 mechanical: \\u0060project add\\u0060, \\u0060project init\\u0060 and \\u0060project set\\u0060 all re-render, and nobody installs an Atlassian CLI for a repository that has never seen Jira. **The install owns the canonical skill set** at \\u0060~/.hall9k/skills\\u0060, published by \\u0060h9k install\\u0060 (from this repository\\u0027s \\u0060.claude/skills\\u0060 today, from release artefacts once backlog 42 lands) - IDEA-skill-layer\\u0027s Tension 8 ruling that a skill the machinery requires is part of the machinery and ships as self-contained as the binaries. A project\\u0027s \\u0060skills/\\u0060 entries are **symlinks into that directory** and \\u0060.claude/skills/\\u0060 is a second layer of symlinks into \\u0060skills/\\u0060, so republishing the install updates every project\\u0027s platform skills in one move, a project-specific skill is a real directory that re-seeding never touches, and there is never a second copy of a skill\\u0027s content to drift. Side-by-side duplicate content directories were rejected outright at the discovery: two copies that can drift means one of them is lying. **The dispatcher composes the home into the briefing.** When a task\\u0027s project has a home, \\u0060AgentPromptBuilder\\u0060 names it, its generated \\u0060AGENTS.md\\u0060, its \\u0060skills/\\u0060 (each with its frontmatter description) and its \\u0060tasks/\\u0060, \\u0060ideas/\\u0060 and \\u0060repo/\\u0060 alongside the repo skills \\u0060DiscoverRepoSkills\\u0060 already hands over; a repo skill of the same name wins, because the repo tier is the more specific one. That is the discovery\\u0027s dispatch-composition ruling: a dispatched agent never hunts for context. It is also what makes the generic \\u0060skills/\\u0060 genuinely model-agnostic - \\u0022read this file first\\u0022 is the one instruction every runtime understands, so nothing depends on any vendor\\u0027s directory-walking behaviour, and native discovery in the home stays a nicety for interactive sessions rather than a load-bearing assumption. **Does this block the later vision?** No, and it is the bridge to it: the home is the boundary a from-anywhere session navigates into, the place the task and idea renders (backlog 48) and the relocated runs (backlog 49) will land, and the unit a project-move or a shared-room migration operates on. The P2P layer\\u0027s lazy, claim-triggered materialisation (#45, \\u00A715 row 20) is unaffected - it now has an explicit sibling to be the eager half of, and one place that already knows what a materialised project looks like.\u0022,\u0022OriginIncident\u0022:null,\u0022Supersedes\u0022:[],\u0022Provenance\u0022:{\u0022RecordedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022RunId\u0022:null,\u0022TaskId\u0022:null,\u0022Attendance\u0022:\u0022Unobserved\u0022,\u0022IsFromRun\u0022:false},\u0022RecordedAt\u0022:\u00222026-09-22T13:15:38.803749\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022LegacyId\u0022:\u0022Decisions Log #76\u0022}","originEventId":"441f6740-2451-40a3-bee7-8578ae364b09","originSequence":58874,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-09-22T13:15:39.710949+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"},{"streamId":"01a0c941-fb35-749f-94bc-d5b053e254bc","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Decision.DecisionRecorded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0c941-fb35-749f-94bc-d5b053e254bc\u0022,\u0022Scope\u0022:\u0022Project\u0022,\u0022ScopeId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Statement\u0022:\u0022**Tasks and ideas render as markdown files in the project home, rewritten by a sweep rather than a per-event handler** (2026-08-23, backlog 48; slice 2 of the project-centred structure, idea 64e4ebd2): the store stays the record, \\u0060\\u003Chome\\u003E/tasks/\\u003Cshortid\\u003E-\\u003Cslug\\u003E/task.md\\u0060 and \\u0060\\u003Chome\\u003E/ideas/\\u003Cshortid\\u003E-\\u003Cslug\\u003E/idea.md\\u0060 are a browsable mirror rewritten whenever the daemon next looks. **The render is a pure function of a document\\u0027s current state, not an event log entry**, so \\u0022driven from the daemon\\u0027s event handling\\u0022 is a sweep over \\u0060TaskDetails\\u0060/\\u0060IdeaDetails\\u0060 - the same shape \\u0060DispatchLoop\\u0060 and \\u0060CardPublicationLoop\\u0060 already use, woken by the shared doorbell and backstopped by a poll interval - rather than a new per-event Wolverine handler; a write only touches disk when the rendered bytes actually differ from what is already there, so a sweep that finds nothing new costs one query per project and the daemon-start reconciliation pass is not a separate code path, it is just the first sweep. **The file format matches \\u0060h9k task add/revise --file\\u0060 exactly**, because it has to: \\u0060task.md\\u0060\\u0027s frontmatter is the readiness contract (objective, criteria, type, model, blocked-by, all as short ids) a human edits and applies back with \\u0060h9k task revise \\u003Cid\\u003E --file\\u0060, and the **body carries only the agent context and nothing else** - no state, no PR link, no conversation - because anything else placed there would round-trip into \\u0060AgentContext\\u0060 on the next revise and silently corrupt it with rendered status noise. Everything else worth showing (state, id, external reference) is frontmatter the parser already ignores as an unrecognized key, including the one-line \\u0022generated, do not hand-edit\\u0022 notice, which lives inside the frontmatter block for the same reason: the parser requires line one to be \\u0060---\\u0060 verbatim, so nothing can precede it. \\u0060idea.md\\u0060 has no such parser to protect - \\u0060h9k idea revise\\u0060 takes the note as a plain argument, not a file - so its header says so and tells the human to paste the body back rather than pointing at a flag that does not exist. **A task or idea\\u0027s directory is named from its *current* objective/text, recomputed every sweep**; a revision that reworded either is what moves the directory, via \\u0060Directory.Move\\u0060 carrying \\u0060workspace/\\u0060 with it, rather than a rename event on the stream. **Orphan reconciliation is conservative**: a directory whose whole \\u0060\\u003Cshortid\\u003E-\\u003Cslug\\u003E\\u0060 name matches nothing the store still knows about is removed outright only when it holds nothing but the generated file and an empty \\u0060workspace/\\u0060; anything with real material in \\u0060workspace/\\u0060 is marked with an \\u0060ORPHANED.md\\u0060 note and never deleted; a sweep is not a human\\u0027s judgment call about what to throw away. Matching is by the whole name rather than the short-id prefix alone, because a prefix match would treat a stale duplicate left behind by an interrupted rename as live just for sharing an id with the directory that is actually current. **An idea renders only once it has a project with a materialised home** - an idea is commonly project-less at capture (Decisions Log #35), and its discovery workspace stays exactly where it is today, at the global \\u0060~/.hall9k/ideas/\\u003Cid\\u003E/workspace\\u0060; relocating it under the project home is backlog 48\\u0027s own DISCOVERY.md slice 3 (\\u0022Relocations\\u0022), deliberately not this task\\u0027s. **Does this block the later vision?** No: the sweep shape is the platform\\u0027s established reactive pattern, so a later true tagged commit becomes a GitHub release, and GitHub is the only host \\u2014 release binaries carry their own checksums, and \\u0060h9k install\\u0060 grew a second, non-repo source rather than a separate installer** (2026-08-23, backlog 42, gaps 1 and 2 of \\u0060IDEA-installation-and-materialisation.md\\u0060): \\u0060.github/workflows/release.yml\\u0060 triggers on a \\u0060v*\\u0060 tag, publishes \\u0060h9k\\u0060 and \\u0060h9kd\\u0060 self-contained (not single-file \\u2014 Wolverine/Marten\\u0027s runtime codegen wants ordinary assembly loading, and self-contained already drops the .NET-SDK-and-runtime requirement without that risk) for \\u0060osx-arm64\\u0060, \\u0060win-x64\\u0060, and \\u0060linux-x64\\u0060, bundles the canonical skill set from \\u0060.claude/skills\\u0060 into each platform\\u0027s payload, and publishes one release carrying every platform\\u0027s archive plus a single \\u0060checksums.txt\\u0060.
